summary_of_interaction: Hon Phil Goff questioned the Prime Minister about his statement that most families' wages are rising faster than inflation. The Prime Minister defended his statement with statistics but was challenged by Hon Phil Goff with contrary evidence and reports. The interaction was marked by interruptions and points of order, with the Speaker intervening to maintain order.
asked_by: Hon PHIL GOFF (Leader of the Opposition)
Example_statements: ['Hon PHIL GOFF: Does he stand by his statement to the House yesterday: “The reason that families should take some comfort is that, by and large, for the most part, their wages are rising faster than the rate of inflation.”', 'Rt Hon JOHN KEY: Yes, and I will explain carefully to the member why the quote in the first part of his question is correct.', 'Hon Phil Goff: Is the Prime Minister, therefore, telling New Zealand families that they are wrong when they believe that the cost of everything is going up, which is leaving them less well off than they were a year ago because most of them have not had wage rises?']

summary_of_interaction: Amy Adams asked the Minister of Finance about international reports on the economy. The Minister responded with details about credit ratings and economic conditions. The opposition challenged the Minister on differing views of economic recovery and inequality, leading to a point of order and the Speaker's intervention.
Example_statements: ['Amy Adams: What international reports has he received on the economy?', 'Hon BILL ENGLISH: In recent weeks I have been able to speak to all three credit-rating agencies.', 'Hon David Cunliffe: In light of these reports, who is correct: the Prime Minister, who described New Zealand’s economic recovery as “aggressive”, or Reserve Bank governor Bollard, who described it in the Finance and Expenditure Committee today as “fragile”?']

summary_of_interaction: Hon David Cunliffe questioned the Minister of Finance about the causes of inflation and government actions to control it. The Minister defended the government's position and tax policies. The opposition challenged the Minister on wage increases and the impact of government policies on workers, leading to a tense exchange.
Example_statements: ['Hon DAVID CUNLIFFE: What were the main price rises that led to the 1.1 percent inflation surge in the September 2010 quarter and how has the Government acted to control those price rises?', 'Hon BILL ENGLISH: First of all, it is not at all apparent that inflation has surged.', 'Hon David Cunliffe: How does he reconcile his claim that New Zealanders seem to be enjoying record wage increases with widespread job losses in the manufacturing, retail, and construction sectors?']

summary_of_interaction: Jo Goodhew asked the Minister of Agriculture about new initiatives to support water augmentation schemes. The Minister responded with details about new grants and changes to eligibility criteria. The opposition questioned the Government's priorities regarding rural water assistance, leading to a defense of the Government's focus on productive investment.
answered_by: Hon Dr NICK SMITH (Minister for the Environment) on behalf of the Minister of Agriculture
Example_statements: ['Jo Goodhew: What new initiatives is MAF taking to support water augmentation schemes around New Zealand?', 'Hon Dr NICK SMITH: Today the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry has announced five new schemes, which are to receive Government support of $1.9 million from the Community Irrigation Fund for technical design work.', 'Hon Damien O’Connor: Will the Government reinstate the $80 million taken from the Drinking-water Assistance Programme put in place to help rural communities access safe drinking-water?']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Trevor Mallard asked the Minister of Labour about the Government's policy on the 90-day trial period in employment agreements. The Minister denied it being the default provision and defended the legislation despite judicial criticism. The Speaker intervened to clarify the appropriateness of commenting on court judgments.
Example_statements: ['Hon TREVOR MALLARD: Is it Government policy for the 90-day scheme to be the default provision in all new employment agreements?', 'Hon KATE WILKINSON: No.', 'Hon TREVOR MALLARD: Does the Government agree with Chief Judge Colgan, who said in paragraph 48 of his judgment in the Smith 90-day case that sections 67A and 67B remove access to justice?']

summary_of_interaction: Hilary Calvert asked the Attorney-General about his amendment to the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Bill regarding free public access. The Attorney-General referred to existing clauses protecting recreational activities. The Speaker ruled the Minister's answer reasonable despite the questioner's dissatisfaction.
Example_statements: ['Hilary Calvert: Will his amendment to the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Bill to ensure that public access to the foreshore and seabed is free, allow for mum, dad and the children to go to the beach for a picnic, a paddle, and to build a sandcastle below the line of mean high water springs so that they won’t be charged for the privilege; if not, why not?', 'Hon CHRISTOPHER FINLAYSON: The bill as already drafted protects recreational activities in or on the common marine and coastal area.', 'Hilary Calvert: I raise a point of order, Mr Speaker. The Minister did not answer the question at all.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon David Parker asked the Minister for Land Information about the number of farms or forests awaiting Overseas Investment Office consent. The Minister explained the legal constraints on declining sales and defended recent decisions. The opposition challenged the Minister on discretion and delays, with the Minister emphasizing adherence to the law.
answered_by: Hon MAURICE WILLIAMSON (Minister for Land Information)
Example_statements: ['Hon DAVID PARKER: How many farms or forests worth $1 million or more are currently the subject of Overseas Investment Office consent?', 'Hon MAURICE WILLIAMSON: Twenty-two.', 'Hon David Parker: Given the Prime Minister’s stated concern about the sale of large tracts of dairy land to overseas buyers, and the breadth of the Minister’s existing discretion to decline, why did the Minister not decline the largest-ever, at $34 million, sale of some of New Zealand’s largest dairy farms to overseas interests just 2 weeks ago?']

summary_of_interaction: Metiria Turei asked the Minister of Finance about closing the wage gap with Australia and the role of unions. The Minister emphasized productivity and economic incentives. The opposition challenged the Government's policies on union access and minimum wage, leading to a debate on economic fairness and worker rights.
Example_statements: ['Metiria Turei: Does he still want to close the wage gap with Australia; and if so, what role does he consider unions will have in closing that gap?', 'Hon BILL ENGLISH: Yes, unions will have a role in assisting to boost productivity in the workplace.', 'Metiria Turei: How will restricting union access to workplaces help to narrow the wage gap with Australia?']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Steve Chadwick asked the Minister of Conservation about support for the Director-General's vision. The Minister expressed agreement with the vision and emphasized the link between conservation and business. The opposition questioned the Minister on environmental decisions, with the Minister clarifying joint decision-making processes.
Example_statements: ['Hon STEVE CHADWICK: Does she support the Director-General of the Department of Conservation and his vision for the future of conservation in New Zealand?', 'Hon KATE WILKINSON: Yes, and in the statement of intent I agree with the vision that “New Zealand is the greatest living space on Earth.”', 'Hon Steve Chadwick: Given her agreement, why is she, then, giving the energy Minister, who has the opposite intention, the power to sign off on mineral exploration permits in the conservation estate?']

summary_of_interaction: Simon Bridges asked the Minister of Justice about changes to the law relating to jurors. The Minister explained changes to improve jurors' privacy and safety by removing addresses from jury lists, balancing privacy and fair trial rights. The interaction was straightforward and informative.
Example_statements: ['Simon Bridges: What changes, if any, is the Government making to the law relating to jurors?', 'Hon SIMON POWER: I am pleased to report to the House that the Government is making changes to improve jurors’ privacy and safety by removing the addresses of potential jurors from jury lists.', 'Simon Bridges: How will the changes depart from existing law?']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Chris Carter asked the Minister of Education about progress on implementing national standards. The Minister expressed satisfaction but acknowledged room for improvement and explained moderation processes. The opposition challenged the Minister on consistency and communication with schools, leading to a request to table a letter.
Example_statements: ['Hon CHRIS CARTER: Is she satisfied with the progress being made to implement national standards?', 'Hon ANNE TOLLEY: Yes, but as the member well knows, there is always room for improvement.', 'Hon Chris Carter: Could she explain to the House the rationale for sending all State and State-integrated primary and intermediate schools a letter on 8 October instructing them to put into their school charters new reporting targets for national standards by the beginning of the 2011 school year, when the criteria for defining and moderating those targets have yet to be defined on a national basis?']

summary_of_interaction: John Hayes asked the Minister of Civil Defence about national efforts to assist New Zealanders to 'Get Ready' and 'Get Thru' disasters. The Minister described Exercise Tangaroa and regional activities including tsunami siren tests. The interaction was informative and straightforward.
answered_by: Hon JOHN CARTER (Minister of Civil Defence)
Example_statements: ['John Hayes: What is happening throughout New Zealand to assist the nation to “Get Ready” and “Get Thru”?', 'Hon JOHN CARTER: Today Exercise Tangaroa is being held. Across the regions and nationally, this exercise will put us to the test and will be used to assess the capability of civil defence.', 'John Hayes: What is happening in Wellington to “Get Ready” and “Get Thru”?']

summary_of_interaction: Dr Jian Yang asked the Minister of Finance about the Government's fiscal approach and its impact on New Zealanders. The Minister defended the approach, citing a surplus and ongoing investments in public services. The interaction included a challenge from Rt Hon Winston Peters about spending cuts, which the Minister addressed by emphasizing prudent expenditure management.
Example_statements: ['Dr Jian Yang: Does he stand by his statement regarding the Government’s fiscal approach that “we decided to support the most vulnerable, maintain benefits and focus on better public services, rather than cut spending”?', 'Hon Bill English: Yes, and a measure of the reasonable effectiveness of that approach has been that in 2014-15 the Government did achieve a surplus despite having, at one stage, a deficit of minus 9 percent of GDP.', 'Rt Hon Winston Peters: Why did the Minister agree to the questioner’s statement “rather than cut spending” when there have been in excess of 58 spending cuts, including cutting the funding contributions to the New Zealand Superannuation Fund?']

summary_of_interaction: Andrew Little questioned the Prime Minister about overseas ownership of New Zealand land, challenging the Government's record on land sales to foreign buyers. The Prime Minister defended the Government's policies and approvals, citing job creation and economic benefits. The exchange was marked by repeated challenges and rebuttals, with interruptions and a tense tone.
Example_statements: ['Andrew Little: Does he stand by his statement made five years ago that “Looking four, five, ten years into the future I’d hate to see New Zealanders as tenants in their own country”?', 'Rt Hon John Key: Yes. Although the Government welcomes investment that creates jobs and growth in New Zealand, we do not want to see excessive rural land sold to overseas buyers.', 'Andrew Little: Has his Government’s decision to approve the sale of 270,000 hectares—five times the size of urban Auckland—made more New Zealanders tenants in their own land—yes or no?']

summary_of_interaction: Simon O’Connor asked the Minister of Health about the expected increase in referrals from B4 School Checks for obesity-related advice following a childhood obesity package announcement. The Minister confirmed the increase and outlined the comprehensive plan. The interaction included interjections and a point of order, with a generally polite but occasionally tense tone.
answered_by: Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman (Minister of Health)
Example_statements: ['Simon O’Connor: Can he confirm the number of referrals from B4 School Checks for obesity-related advice and support is expected to treble as a result of the childhood obesity package announced yesterday?', 'Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman: Yes, I can. Yesterday I announced a comprehensive plan to reduce childhood obesity.', 'Sue Moroney: Does he agree with the World Health Organization that there is a mounting body of evidence showing breastfeeding plays a role in protecting children against obesity, and, therefore, will he recommend support for the Labour Party’s proposal to extend paid parental leave to 26 weeks so mums can aim to breastfeed to 6 months, as recommended by the World Health Organization?']

summary_of_interaction: Rt Hon Winston Peters asked the Minister of Transport about the Government's discussions with KiwiRail regarding the Northland rail network. The Minister responded that KiwiRail considers the economics challenging but there are no plans to close the line. Peters pressed on maintenance and private business discussions, with the Minister emphasizing investment and lack of demand for rail freight. The tone was tense with interruptions.
Example_statements: ['Rt Hon Winston Peters: What discussions has the National-led Government had with KiwiRail about plans for railways in Northland?', 'Hon Simon Bridges: I meet with KiwiRail regularly, and I discuss ways to improve the productivity of the rail network around New Zealand—that, of course, includes Northland.', 'Rt Hon Winston Peters: Is it the Government’s intention to close the rail line going up north from Auckland?', 'Hon Simon Bridges: As I say, there are no plans to do that.']

summary_of_interaction: James Shaw asked the Minister for Climate Change Issues about instructions to the New Zealand delegation at the Bonn Climate Change Conference, focusing on New Zealand's contribution to the Green Climate Fund. The Minister defended New Zealand's international contributions, citing investments in the Pacific and other initiatives. Shaw challenged the low per capita contribution, with the Minister emphasizing overall contributions. The tone was polite but with some challenge.
answered_by: Hon Simon Bridges (Associate Minister for Climate Change Issues)
Example_statements: ['James Shaw: What specific instructions has he given to the New Zealand delegation to take to the Bonn Climate Change Conference this week?', 'Hon Simon Bridges: The delegation will be negotiating at the climate change meeting in Bonn this week on the basis of the existing Cabinet mandate.', 'James Shaw: Do these instructions include reference to the fact that New Zealand’s contribution to the Green Climate Fund sits at just 88c per capita, compared with the average contribution of $12.46 per capita from other nations?']

summary_of_interaction: Phil Twyford asked the Minister for Building and Housing about the Government's position on banning non-resident foreign buyers from purchasing existing homes, referencing the Australian housing policy. The Minister defended the Government's position, citing the failure of the Australian policy and emphasizing supply as the key issue. Twyford challenged the Minister's statistics on house price growth, which the Minister disputed. The tone was confrontational with interruptions.
answered_by: Hon Dr Nick Smith (Minister for Building and Housing)
Example_statements: ['Phil Twyford: Is the reason he does not support banning non-resident foreign buyers from purchasing existing homes, that he agrees with the Prime Minister that the Australian Government’s housing policy has been “spectacularly unsuccessful”?', 'Hon Dr Nick Smith: The reason the Government does not support bans on foreign buyers is that they are shown not to work.', 'Phil Twyford: Can he confirm that CoreLogic Australia’s data shows that Sydney was the Australian city with the fastest house price growth in the last year, at 16.7 percent, yet Auckland house prices in the same period went up 22.6 percent, meaning that Auckland house prices were going up 35 percent faster than Sydney’s?']

summary_of_interaction: Alfred Ngaro asked the Minister of Transport about progress on the Waterview Connection Project in Auckland. The Minister reported the completion of the second tunnel and highlighted the project's benefits for Auckland's population and economy. The interaction was informative and polite.
Example_statements: ['Alfred Ngaro: What recent reports has he seen on progress with the Government’s Waterview Connection Project in Auckland?', 'Hon Simon Bridges: Yesterday Alice, the world’s tenth-largest tunnel-boring machine, completed the second of the twin three-lane tunnels, marking a major step towards completing the Government’s $1.4 billion Waterview Connection project.', 'Alfred Ngaro: How will the Waterview Connection benefit road users and support the future growth of Auckland’s population and economy?']

summary_of_interaction: Kevin Hague asked the Minister of Health about the effectiveness of interventions against childhood obesity. The Minister expressed confidence in the comprehensive package. Hague questioned the focus on individuals rather than societal factors and the absence of a fizzy-drinks tax. The Minister responded with evidence-based reasoning. The tone was polite with some challenge.
answered_by: Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman (Minister of Health)
Example_statements: ['Kevin Hague: Is he confident that the interventions announced yesterday will be effective against the key environmental drivers of obesity, given that one-third of New Zealand children are overweight?', 'Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman: Yes. I think that being virtually the only country with a national obesity target and a comprehensive evidence-based life course package for children will be effective.', 'Kevin Hague: Why is the Minister not considering a fizzy-drinks tax when the Prime Minister’s own Chief Science Advisor, Sir Peter Gluckman, has strongly recommended one?']

summary_of_interaction: Jacinda Ardern asked the Minister of Health about his colleague Anne Tolley's statement on pies and healthy eating guidelines in schools. The Minister defended the decision and the current approach. Ardern challenged the Minister on contradictions and the effectiveness of the B4 School Check target. The Minister responded with statistics and expert advice. The tone was tense with interruptions.
answered_by: Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman (Minister of Health)
Example_statements: ['Jacinda Ardern: Does he agree with his colleague Hon Anne Tolley’s statement that children who need “that instant hit of carbohydrates, a pie might not be a bad thing,” and her subsequent decision to scrap healthy eating guidelines in schools in 2009?', 'Hon Dr Jonathan Coleman: Yes, I think the decision was widely welcomed by schools at the time.', 'Jacinda Ardern: Is he now contradicting himself, given that he said in 2005 that “I can show you primary schools … where kids have a $1 pie for breakfast from the school tuck shop, then follow up with more of the same for lunch. That’s what has to stop.”?']

summary_of_interaction: Todd Barclay asked the Minister for Communications about recent announcements on rural broadband connectivity. The Minister outlined ambitious targets and international comparisons. Rt Hon Winston Peters challenged the Minister on budget and infrastructure upgrades in Northland. The Minister defended the Government's record and funding. The tone was polite with some challenge.
Example_statements: ['Todd Barclay: What recent announcements has she made regarding rural connectivity?', 'Hon Amy Adams: Earlier this month I announced that the Government was adopting ambitious targets for rural connectivity.', 'Rt Hon Winston Peters: If any of that is true, what budget has been set aside to upgrade existing infrastructure, including broadband cabinets in Northland, to ensure that existing businesses and households regain secure and reliable internet speeds?']

summary_of_interaction: Hon James Shaw asked the Minister of Finance about government support for workers needing leave due to COVID-19. The Minister explained the removal of revenue drop tests for the Leave Support Scheme to help workers self-isolate without financial penalty. The discussion focused on ensuring workers are supported to get tested and isolate without using annual leave.
Example_statements: ['Is the Government supporting working people who need to take leave due to COVID-19; if so, how?', 'Yesterday, I announced that Cabinet has agreed to remove the revenue drop and negatively impacted tests for the COVID-19 Leave Support Scheme.', 'No. The leave scheme is available so that businesses with workers who have been told by health officials or their medical practitioner to self-isolate will receive the equivalent of the wage subsidy to cover the person’s wages for the time they cannot be at work.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Judith Collins questioned the Prime Minister about the source of the COVID-19 outbreak in Auckland and weaknesses in border procedures. The Prime Minister responded that investigations are ongoing and explained the testing strategy and challenges faced. The interaction included scrutiny over testing coverage and government preparedness.
Example_statements: ['What advice, if any, has she received on the most likely way COVID-19 entered Auckland, causing the lockdown which began on 12 August, and what weaknesses, if any, have officials identified in border procedures which may have left New Zealand vulnerable to fresh outbreaks of COVID-19?', 'To date, we have not established the source of the current cluster, but investigations continue.', 'Why have not all border-facing staff been tested, eight weeks after her Government said they would be tested?']

summary_of_interaction: Greg O’Connor asked the Minister of Finance about recent government actions to support the economy under COVID-19 restrictions. The Minister detailed the new wage subsidy scheme and other financial supports to cushion economic impact. The discussion emphasized the link between public health measures and economic recovery.
Example_statements: ['What recent actions has he taken to support the New Zealand economy under the current COVID-19 restrictions?', 'Yesterday, I announced criteria for a new nationwide wage subsidy covering the period that Auckland is at COVID-19 alert level 3.', 'The new wage subsidy scheme helps cushion the blow to households and businesses while public health measures take effect.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Gerry Brownlee questioned the Minister of Housing about testing of managed isolation and quarantine (MIQ) staff and the government's border management. The Minister acknowledged issues with testing coverage and explained the steps taken to improve testing rates. The exchange involved challenges on government preparedness and response.
Example_statements: ['Does she think the public should be concerned that post the 23 June announcement by the Minister of Health that “a testing strategy to keep New Zealand safe” with priority testing for MIQ staff and international and maritime crews was not comprehensively put in place, despite the Prime Minister stating last week that testing was happening all the way through?', 'Testing was taking place after the decisions in June and further announcements in July.', 'Prior to Friday we had a voluntary system alongside surveillance testing, not a mandatory system that did not come into place until the order came into being.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Paul Goldsmith asked the Minister of Finance about the total estimated cost of the COVID-19 resurgence to the economy and government. The Minister provided estimates of economic impact and government expenditure on wage subsidies. The discussion also touched on government preparedness and border security measures.
Example_statements: ['What is the total estimated cost, to both the economy and to the Government, of the re-emergence of COVID-19 in the community?', 'There is a wide range of estimates of the total cost to the economy from economists, ranging from an impact on GDP of $300 million per week to about $500 million to $600 million per week.', 'We absolutely want all New Zealanders to be confident that if they do need to take a test and they do need to self-isolate, they will have some support for their income.']

summary_of_interaction: Kiritapu Allan asked the Minister of Education about government support for students affected by the shift to alert level 3 in Auckland. The Minister described funding for distance learning, provision of digital devices, and support for senior students to attend school with safety measures. The interaction focused on educational continuity during restrictions.
Example_statements: ['What steps is the Government taking to support students whose learning has been disrupted by the shift to COVID-19 alert level 3 in Auckland?', 'The Ministry of Education has been purchasing the limited stock of fit-for-education computer devices that are available in New Zealand.', 'Senior secondary school students in years 12 and 13 can come back into school during level 3, providing all of the relevant protections are put in place.']

summary_of_interaction: Dr Shane Reti questioned the Minister of Health about testing rates of border staff and the accuracy of information received. The Minister confirmed incomplete testing and regular updates on testing progress. The discussion included transparency and accountability regarding border testing.
Example_statements: ['Does he stand by his statement regarding testing of border staff that “it has not been happening at the rates (a) we have asked for and (b) we were told”?', 'I was told that by the Ministry of Health, and, yes, I did receive that in writing.', 'Yes, I asked for detailed breakdowns on a very regular basis of all of the testing taking place across the country.']

summary_of_interaction: Chris Bishop asked the Minister of Health about the government’s testing plan for maritime transport workers and its implementation. The Minister explained the testing strategy, challenges in testing all sea border workers, and efforts to increase testing. The exchange focused on border security and testing logistics.
Example_statements: ['What does the Government’s resurgence plan for COVID-19 say about testing those involved in maritime transport, if anything, and is he satisfied with the implementation of that plan?', 'Testing at the maritime border includes regular ongoing testing of port workers who have contact with ships’ crew.', 'It is not possible to test all of the people at the sea border.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon Ron Mark asked the Minister of Internal Affairs about a new lottery fund to support communities affected by COVID-19. The Minister explained the fund’s purpose, funding source, and its non-impact on other lottery allocations. The interaction was informative and supportive.
Example_statements: ['What recent announcements has she made regarding lottery funding and local communities in light of COVID-19?', 'A new lottery fund worth $40 million has been established to focus on community and social initiatives in the wake of COVID-19.', 'This COVID-19 fund will not affect the allocation of funding to other distribution committees.']

summary_of_interaction: Hon David Bennett asked the Minister of Agriculture about exemptions for primary sector workers crossing level 3 boundaries and the application of essential services definitions. The Minister explained the health orders, exemption processes, and ongoing engagement with industry. The discussion addressed balancing COVID-19 risk and essential sector operations.
Example_statements: ['Why did the Director-General of MPI tell Beef + Lamb New Zealand and the Meat Industry Association on Wednesday last week that the same definition of essential services used during the last lockdown would apply again in this lockdown, and are farmers also required to get a Ministry of Health exemption to cross the level 3 boundary for work purposes?', 'Yes, exemptions are required to cross the level 3 boundary for work purposes.', 'We have been trying to manage that to reduce the risk of spread but to allow the sensible movement of people where absolutely essential.']

summary_of_interaction: Ginny Andersen asked the Attorney-General about the COVID-19 Public Health Response Act 2020 and its role in the government’s pandemic response. The Attorney-General explained the Act’s improvements over the 1956 Health Act, democratic oversight, and its necessity. The exchange highlighted legal frameworks supporting targeted COVID-19 measures.
Example_statements: ['How has the COVID-19 Public Health Response Act 2020 supported the Government’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic?', 'The COVID-19 Public Health Response Act has enabled the Government to implement the resurgence response plan quickly, with democratic oversight.', 'The Act confers the power to make orders on Ministers—accountable to Parliament—acting on advice from officials, rather than orders being made directly by officials.']

summary_of_interaction: Nancy Lu asked the Acting Minister of Finance about recent economic reports, focusing on inflation and its drivers. The Minister responded with detailed statistics on CPI inflation, its causes, and outlook, emphasizing government efforts to control inflation and its impact on families and businesses. The tone was informative and polite.
answered_by: Hon Chris Bishop (Acting Minister of Finance)
Example_statements: ['Nancy Lu: What recent reports has she seen on the economy?', 'Hon CHRIS BISHOP: Yesterday, Stats New Zealand released the latest figures for the Consumers Price Index—the CPI...', 'Nancy Lu: What is driving the current bump in annual CPI inflation?', 'Hon CHRIS BISHOP: Almost a third of the annual inflation figure was due to food items—including dairy, meat, and fruit and vegetables...']

summary_of_interaction: Rt Hon Chris Hipkins questioned the Prime Minister on inflation rates and government responsibility. The Prime Minister responded by comparing current inflation to previous government levels and emphasized government policies. The interaction was tense with multiple points of order and interruptions.
asked_by: Rt Hon Chris Hipkins (Leader of the Opposition)
Example_statements: ['Rt Hon Chris Hipkins: What was the annual rate of inflation one year ago and what is it today?', 'Rt Hon CHRISTOPHER LUXON: What I can tell the member is that it’s not 7.3 percent, which is what it was under his Government.', 'Rt Hon Chris Hipkins: What proportion of current inflation is driven by the increase in Government prices?', 'Rt Hon CHRISTOPHER LUXON: I don’t have that number with me.']

summary_of_interaction: Laura McClure asked the Minister for Children about government actions to improve outcomes for children, support caregivers, social workers, and improve standards in Oranga Tamariki residences. The Minister responded with detailed information on government priorities, achievements, and ongoing initiatives. The tone was polite and constructive.

summary_of_interaction: Hon Barbara Edmonds questioned the Acting Minister of Finance on inflation control statements and rising prices affecting workers. The Minister defended government actions and investments, acknowledged challenges, and encouraged unions to bargain in good faith. The tone was somewhat confrontational with interruptions.

summary_of_interaction: Chlöe Swarbrick asked the Prime Minister about his government’s support for workers, pay conditions, and safe working environments. The Prime Minister emphasized government investments and urged unions to return to bargaining. The interaction was tense with interruptions and points of order.

summary_of_interaction: Ryan Hamilton asked the Minister of Transport about announcements on the Roads of National Significance programme. The Minister detailed funding, endorsed investment cases, and ongoing construction projects. The tone was polite and informative despite some interruptions.

answered_by: Hon Brooke Van Velden (Minister for Workplace Relations and Safety)

What I would encourage them to do is to get back around the bargaining table.']

summary_of_interaction: Carl Bates asked the Minister of Education about support for students with higher and complex needs. The Minister described government initiatives including the extended curriculum and professional development for specialist teachers. The tone was informative and polite.

summary_of_interaction: Debbie Ngarewa-Packer asked the Prime Minister about Māori customary rights to the foreshore and seabed and government legislation.
